Description

Kinase suppressor of Ras 1 (KSR1) is a pseudokinase related to RAF that binds MEK1 and MEK2 constitutively [1, 2]. In resting cells 14-3-3 holds it in the cytoplasm, bound to two phosphoserines of KSR1, Ser311 and Ser406 of the human protein (Ser297 and Ser392 of the mouse protein studied) [3, 4]. C-TAK1 (MARK3) phosphorylates Ser406 [4]. When growth factors activate RAS, protein phosphatase 2A removes this phosphate, 14-3-3 is released and KSR1 moves with its MEK to the plasma membrane [4, 5]. There KSR1 pairs side to side with BRAF bound to RAS, a pairing that the MEK on KSR1 and the N-terminal regions of both proteins promote [2, 6-8]. In this model BRAF in the pair switches the conformation of the MEK held by KSR1, so that a second, catalytic RAF phosphorylates it, and the KSR1 complex raises MEK activation [2, 7]. Mice without KSR1 develop normally but activate ERK less, and the large complexes of KSR, MEK and ERK are lost from their cells [9].
